title: Infinitesimal pushout gluing of proper flat curves
statement: On schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Arrows in $\mathcal C(T)$ are $T$-isomorphisms and pullback is cartesian base change; arrows over $T'\to T$ are isomorphisms $X'\cong X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Let $T\to T'$ be a thickening (a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism on underlying spaces), and let $T\to S$ be affine. Let $S'=S\amalg_TT'$ be their pushout in schemes. The restriction functor $\mathcal C(S')\to\mathcal C(S)\times_{\mathcal C(T)}\mathcal C(T')$ is an equivalence of groupoids: pairs of families with a specified isomorphism over $T$ glue, uniquely up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the gluing data. The fibre product here has triples $(a,b,\phi:a|_T\cong b|_T)$ as objects and pairs of isomorphisms commuting with $\phi$ as arrows. Here finite presentation for algebraic spaces means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, with quasi-separatedness meaning that the diagonal is quasi-compact. The geometric fibre of an algebraic space is the same formula $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(t)}$, using fibre products of algebraic spaces [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; its topology is the quotient topology from an etale scheme atlas.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout] to the given span. In its notation $P=S\prime$, so $j:S\to S\prime$ is a thickening and $T=S\times_{S\prime}T\prime$. Moreover each $s\prime\in S\prime$ has exactly one preimage $s\in S$, and $\kappa(s\prime)\cong\kappa(s)$: locally the closed immersion is $A\to A/I$ with $I$ contained in every prime of $A$, and the residue fields at corresponding primes are the same fractions of $A/\mathfrak p$. Thus the same chosen algebraic closure gives compatible geometric points over $s$ and $s\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0D56, last sentence of proof; Tag 07RT.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F(B)$ denote the category of flat locally finitely presented algebraic spaces over $B$, with all $B$-morphisms. By [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-pushout-gluing], restriction gives an equivalence $F:\mathcal F(S\prime)\to\mathcal F(S)\times_{\mathcal F(T)}\mathcal F(T\prime)$. Restriction sends a curve family to curve families: flatness and local finite presentation are part of the stated functor, properness is preserved by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change], and the dimension bound is preserved by [lem-sfb-space-fibre-dimension-base-change] with $d=1$, whose quasi-separatedness hypothesis holds because a proper morphism is separated and a closed immersion is quasi-compact. Properness supplies quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness (a closed diagonal is quasi-compact), so together with local finite presentation each restriction is finitely presented. Thus $F$ restricts to the functor in the statement. The categories $\mathcal C(B)$ are the full subgroupoids on the curve-family objects of $\mathcal F(B)$.

source.place: Tag 0D56, embedding and forward implication; Tag 0D1J, first paragraph, expanded using Tag 07W3.

proof.text: Given an object $(X,Y,\phi)$ of $\mathcal C(S)\times_{\mathcal C(T)}\mathcal C(T\prime)$, regard it as an object of the ambient category of triples. Essential surjectivity in [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-pushout-gluing] gives $W\to S\prime$ flat and locally finitely presented, with isomorphisms $W\times_{S\prime}S\cong X$ and $W\times_{S\prime}T\prime\cong Y$ whose restrictions agree with the specified $\phi$. These are isomorphisms of gluing data, so the original specified identification, not merely the isomorphism classes of $X,Y$, is recovered.

source.place: Tag 0D56 through Tag 0D1J, flat locally finitely presented gluing by Tag 07W3.

proof.text: The inclusion $W_S=W\times_{S\prime}S\to W$ is a thickening. Indeed on an etale affine scheme chart of $W$, it is defined by the image of the ideal of $S$ in $S\prime$; every element of this image is nilpotent, because the original ideal lies in the nilradical. The quotient therefore has the same primes as the chart. Apply [lem-sfb-space-thickening-topological-properties] to the resulting morphism of thickenings $(W_S\subset W)\to(S\subset S\prime)$. Since $W_S\to S$ is isomorphic to the given proper finitely presented $X\to S$, it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, separated and universally closed. All four properties therefore hold for $W\to S\prime$. This map is already locally finitely presented, hence locally of finite type: a finite presentation has finitely many algebra generators. Quasi-compactness then makes it of finite type; separatedness and universal closedness make it proper. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness together with local finite presentation make it finitely presented. This uses no finite-order thickening hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0D1J properness test expanded with Tag 09ZY(3),(4),(6); Tag 03XP, definition-locally-finite-presentation.

proof.text: For every $s\prime\in S\prime$, take its unique preimage $s\in S$ and the common algebraic closure $\Omega$ of their residue fields from step 1. The fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $$W\times_{S\prime}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\cong(W\times_{S\prime}S)\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\cong X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega.$$ Explicitly on any test scheme both sides are pairs of a section of $W$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ having the same map to $S\prime$; the map from $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ factors through $S$. This is an isomorphism of algebraic spaces, so their underlying topological spaces and dimensions agree. The last dimension is at most one by the hypothesis on $X$. Consequently $W\to S\prime$ is a curve family; the isomorphisms of step 3 prove essential surjectivity on curve families, including empty fibres.

source.place: Tag 0D56, final relative-dimension implication; fibre comparison written explicitly.

proof.text: For curve families $W_1,W_2$, any compatible pair of isomorphisms between their restrictions is a morphism between the two ambient triples. Full faithfulness in [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-pushout-gluing] gives a unique ambient morphism $h:W_1\to W_2$ inducing it. Lift the inverse pair to $k:W_2\to W_1$. Faithfulness gives $kh=1$ and $hk=1$, because their restrictions are identities. Thus $h$ is an isomorphism and belongs to $\mathcal C(S\prime)$. This proves full faithfulness on the groupoids. Together with step 5 it proves the equivalence. Two objects equipped with the same specified gluing data consequently have exactly one isomorphism respecting those data; no claim is made that curve families have trivial automorphism groups.

source.place: Tag 0D56, restriction of the ambient equivalence to the full subgroupoid; Hom-set argument expanded.
